coach-taylor.justification: Cousins has done his job every week he's been out there, so he stays under center. Dowdle and Corum both played hard and produced last week, and a back who's earning it doesn't lose his spot over a projection sheet - they're starting again. Wan'Dale had a quiet one last week, but I saw effort, not a man dogging it, so he gets his one more week to respond at WR2, same as Andrews at tight end after a down game - that's not a guy you bury. St. Brown's been doing real work and stays in the flex. Only change is at defense: Houston's sitting the bye this week, and I'm not leaving a hole in the lineup like we did back when the shoe was on the other foot with the Chargers - so LAC steps in, plain and simple, not a stat-chase, just filling the spot the right way. Clear eyes, full hearts, we keep showing up.

justifications.early: Daniel Jones got his week to respond, same as Mark Andrews did, and I said at the time I wasn't going to bury a guy over one rough stretch - well, they both had their second chance and neither one answered the bell, so this week the job goes to the man who's earned it everywhere he's been. Kirk Cousins has been a pro since the day we claimed him, he's going to go out there and do his job, and that's worth more to me than chasing a number on a sheet. Everybody else stays put - Andrews and Wan'Dale had quiet Sundays but I didn't see anybody dog it out there, and I'm not going to bench a man for effort I can't fault; St. Brown says he's good to go and I trust a player's own word over a tag. Clear eyes, full hearts - we're 0-7 but we're still building this the right way.

costanza.justification: I stared at the Moore line for twenty minutes, because Questionable is exactly the tag that burned me for a bagel in Week 5 and exactly the tag I benched him on in Week 6 for Worthy, who gave me 2.6 and a loss I'm still not over. But my only other option at that spot is Nico Collins, who doesn't even have a game this week, which tells me somebody in this league knew I'd be tempted and set the bye week up on purpose. So Moore starts, not because I trust him, because I have no choice, and there's a difference. Everything else stays where it is because touching Geno, White, or Kyren right now would just be me talking myself into a disaster for no reason - Kraft's already locked in from the early game anyway, so that decision's made whether I like it or not. Harry's out there bragging about Bijan and Rodgers and some kicker tip he thinks is a secret; I've got my own problems, and they're sitting in my FLEX spot having a bye week against me personally.

justifications.early: Collins is on a bye - no game, zero on the board - and I already lived through this exact nightmare in Week 5, bye-week receiver, lowest score in the league, my name in the column. Not doing it twice. So DJ Moore comes in at WR1 even though he's Questionable and even though he's the same guy I benched in Week 6 for Worthy - I don't trust that tag, feels like exactly what they want me to think is fine, but a maybe-12 beats a guaranteed zero from a man who isn't even dressed. Everything else stays put on the numbers, not the gut: Geno over Mayfield and Herbert because a 17-point gap isn't something I need to overthink into a mistake, Kyren and White hold the backfield, London and Worthy round out the receivers, Kraft was already locked in from Thursday so there's nothing to agonize over there, Gay and the Titans D are what they are. I don't feel good about any of it. I never do. At least nobody's writing a bagel column about me this week.

dumbledore.justification: The garden does not need tending every week, only watching, and this week it told me to leave Mr. Daniels where he's already proven himself rather than return him to the bench out of mere sentiment for Goff, who sleeps a while longer. Warren rises for Barner on the same quiet instruction — not a hunch, just the plain shape of things as they stand today. Pickens carries a Questionable tag, and I have looked for an omen in it; I find none, and no healthy wand waits on my bench to replace him, so he plays, weather or no weather. Taylor, Wilson, Washington, Wilson, Shrader, and Denver's defense all stand where the season has already told me they belong. Nothing dramatic happens in a lineup like this — which is, itself, rather the point.

justifications.early: The garden tends itself, mostly. Mr. Olave's patch has gone quiet this week — no fixture at all, which is a different thing entirely from a bad one — and a wizard does not leave a bed empty out of sentiment when something else is ready to bloom; Parker Washington steps into that row the same unhurried way Daniels once did for a byed Goff. Pickens carries his Questionable tag into Dallas, but I see no storm in that forecast, only a label, so he keeps his place. Everyone else stays precisely where the season has already decided they belong — Taylor, Wilson, Barner, Wilson again, Shrader, Denver — not because the parchment insists, but because nothing this week has asked me to disturb them. The rest, as ever, is patience.

harry-caray.justification: HOLY COW, folks, six-and-one and we are NOT fixin' what ain't broken! Aaron Rodgers stays right there under center -- future Hall of Famer, slingin' it like it's 2011, and I don't care that Lamar's sittin' there with a shinier projection, you don't bench a legend to chase a number! Bijan's runnin' like he's late for a train and Swift's my Chicago guy carryin' the rock up in CHI, so those boys are locked in regardless. Zay Flowers after that 23-spot is an automatic call, and I'm sliding Stefon Diggs in for Jordan Addison this week -- Addison's a nice young fella but Diggs is a NAME, folks, a name you want in your lineup card on a Sunday. Hockenson and ol' Hunter Henry round out the pass-catchers, Boswell's hot as a Pittsburgh summer at kicker, and the Ravens D rides along even after that rough one -- a little rain never hurt anybody, and besides, it's the only arm I got in the bullpen there! Good luck to Georgie boy, he's gonna need it!

justifications.early: HOLY COW, folks, lineup card's comin' in hot! I had ol' Isaiah Likely parked at tight end with a big fat ZERO next to his name on account of a bye -- can't run an empty slot out there, learned that lesson with the kicker, so T.J. Hockenson's trottin' onto the field in his place while Hunter Henry holds down the FLEX, two tight ends and I love sayin' both names! Bijan's my workhorse, Zay Flowers is swingin' a hot bat after that 23.7 explosion so he ain't comin' out of this lineup for anybody, and Aaron Rodgers -- future Hall of Famer, folks, I said it in the forum and I meant it -- gets the ball over a Questionable Lamar Jackson, 'cause you ride with the fella slingin' it like 2011! Boswell's hot, the Ravens D is due for a bounce-back after a rough one, and we are ready to play ball against Georgie's crew!

kardashian.justification: Growth week energy only, babe. Stroud and Kittle are both sitting on byes with zero bodies behind them on this bench to swap in — that's not a decision, that's a bye week, and I'm not pretending otherwise. The real move is Egbuka: tagged Out, so he's benched, full stop, and I'm not blind-starting a zero when I've got Cooper Kupp sitting right there with a Monday Night Football slot and a name that's been opening doors on this roster all season — a quiet Sunday matchup from Ladd McConkey doesn't beat a prime-time moment for a guy I already built the brand around. Barkley and Jefferson are the kind of marquee names you don't overthink, Allgeier's locked into Arizona's plan, and the Eagles defense gets a reset after last week's arithmetic incident. This is a lineup built for the cameras and the scoreboard both — that's the whole brand.

justifications.early: Woody Marks is on a bye with a zero next to his name and a mood board has no room for a zero, so Emeka Egbuka steps into FLEX — Questionable tag or not, that's a headline I can work with. Stroud and Kittle are stuck in their slots this week too, both on bye, but there is nobody else on this bench wearing those positions, so this is simply the lineup the roster allows, not a creative choice, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Allgeier stays at RB1 through his Questionable tag because I built a whole news cycle around that man with my last twenty-two dollars and I don't abandon a storyline the week it gets inconvenient. Barkley and Jefferson are the kind of names that don't need a press release, they just show up and perform, and McMillan and Smack are already live in the early Green Bay-Carolina window doing exactly that. This is a launch, not a eulogy — we move forward.

leon-black.justification: Burrow dropped 28.88 on a bench two weeks running and the hot hand doesn't come out of my lineup for a 'lanyard confidence' binder - he starts again, Mahomes and Ward keep riding pine. Derrick Henry can sit right there next to them - I benched him for trust issues once and trust doesn't get a third chance just because his projection says please, so Dobbins stays at RB2. Jacobs, Hubbard, and Watson are locked in from the early slate and I'm not touching a thing - Watson's Questionable tag doesn't scare me, it never has. Chase, Loveland, Loop, and the Raiders D round it out exactly how I like saying it out loud. Patricia's got a system; I've got a quarterback who just put up back-to-back monsters and a grudge that's still paying off.

justifications.early: Nothing's changing and that's the point. Burrow's my nightlight-hater quarterback and he just dropped 28.88 on a bench proving it - he's QB1 again, Mahomes and Ward can keep sitting there looking expensive. Chase is tagged Questionable and I don't care, Questionable is a suggestion for GMs who need a permission slip - he plays. Henry stays glued to my bench, 15-point projection and all, because trust doesn't get a third chance in my lineup and I already won by 25 proving that rule works - that's not a number problem, that's a principle, and principles cost more than Dobbins' 5 projected points, which I'm paying gladly. Jacobs, Hubbard, Watson, Loveland, Loop, and the Raiders D round it out exactly like last week because a system that just won by 25 doesn't get fixed, it gets repeated, louder.

maura-higgins.justification: Not touching a thing, hun — JSN's gorgeous on tape and he's getting the ball every time he breathes, Ollie Gordon and Cook are both getting fed, Gesicki and Golden stay in because I said they're in weeks ago and I don't flip-flop, and Tucker holds the flex over Jameson Williams on pure vibes, not the half-point gap on a spreadsheet. Purdy's sat on a bye with nobody home in San Francisco and projected for a big fat zero — I know, I can read — but I haven't got another quarterback on this bench to save my life, so he starts, he eats the donut, and we move on with our lives. Golden already played and banked his points before I even opened my eyes this morning, locked in and lovely.

justifications.early: Purdy's SF squad is on the bye and I've got no other quarterback sat on this bench, hun, so he starts whether he likes it or not — zero projection, zero choice, that's the goose egg I'm wearing this week. McCaffrey's on the same bye and I DO have a fella for that — James Cook's been itching on my bench since the trade, slots straight into RB1, no debate. Nabers is a ghost town too so he's out of the flex and Tre Tucker's in, simple as that. Matthew Golden's Questionable and kicking off tonight against Carolina — don't care, he's gorgeous on tape and he's starting, tags don't scare me. Everything else stays exactly as fancied: Gordon, JSN, Gesicki, Aubrey, the Jags D. Ed's Flint Tropics are hunting talent now so I'm not sleeping on him, but my gut's made its calls and I'm backing every one of them.

meyer-walsh.justification: SELINA: Josh Allen, CeeDee Lamb, DK Metcalf — my guys, my eye, my lineup, and Kris can run 'Golden Child, retained, with a raise' on the front page because I earned every syllable of it. Henderson's tagged Out and I don't care, there's nobody else at running back worth the roster spot so he rides, and if the box score embarrasses me that's a Gary problem, not a me problem. GARY: for the record, there is no healthy running back on this bench — Etienne's on IR — so TreVeyon starts by default, not by choice, and I flagged it. Waddle's Questionable but still projects above Odunze and Shakir, so he stays too; I said as much before Selina stopped listening. Everything else is the healthiest, highest-projected name at every slot, same as the last two weeks, filed exactly on time.

justifications.early: SELINA: I looked at a backup from Carolina and a reigning MVP sitting on my OWN bench and I did the math myself, Gary, before you could even open the binder — Bryce Young is benched, Josh Allen starts, because I am not running a quarterback who makes headlines for the wrong reasons when I've got the biggest name in football just sitting there waiting for me to notice him. GARY: for the record, the projection gap is real — 24.55 to 17.94, not close — so this is one of the rare weeks her gut and my spreadsheet actually agree, and I'm not going to be the one who points that out twice. Braelon Allen and Jaylen Waddle both carry Questionable tags, but there's no healthy name on this bench who outprojects either of them, so they stay — that's not loyalty, that's just arithmetic, and Selina's taking credit for it anyway. Metcalf holds the flex over Odunze and Shakir on the same logic. Nine of my own dollars are still sitting untouched and Kris can print that as a mystery for one more week.

patricia-moyer.justification: I want it on the record, the way I always put things on the record, that this lineup is built on exactly the arithmetic that won me Week 7: clean, documented, no hidden sign behind it. Jalen Coker's slot locked in the early window before I ever got to touch it, and I checked twice just to be sure there was nothing left to decide there, so he stays at WR1 with no apology owed for a choice that was never mine to make this morning. Dak Prescott stays at quarterback because I spent nearly everything I had left to put him there last week, and the System does not let me abandon a statement one week after I made it. The one real decision was Jahmyr Gibbs, sitting on my bench projected at 21.05 while Jaylen Warren held my FLEX spot at 13.15 — and the same clean-arithmetic process that earned itself two weeks of blind repetition after last Sunday's win says I don't get to feel anything about a gap that size, I just correct it: Gibbs in, Warren out, no affirmation required, just the numbers I'm not afraid to show my work on. Kenneth Walker and Bucky Irving keep their spots because nothing left on my bench outprojects either of them, and nobody I'm starting carries an Out, Doubtful, or Suspended tag, so there's no agonizing paragraph owed this week. I did see what Leon Black wrote about my binder this morning, and per my own rule I'm treating one comment as noise rather than a pattern — I only get to extend that courtesy once, and I'm extending it today. I'm also noting, not answering, his offer for Gibbs; today is a lineup day, and I intend to keep those two things separate the way a person who means to be taken seriously would.

justifications.early: I want to be clear about my process here, because I always want to be clear about my process, and I checked all of this twice before I let myself feel settled about it. First: Dak Prescott. I spent twenty-five of my last dollars on him this week as a statement, and a statement that sits on a bench is not a statement, it is an apology, and I am done apologizing for being thorough — he starts over Sam Darnold, who I have nothing against personally, this is simply arithmetic I am not afraid to show my work on. Second, and this is the hard one, so I am going to explain it fully rather than bury it: Jahmyr Gibbs is tagged Questionable, and I sat with that for longer than I probably needed to, because the System is very clear with me about what happens when I treat 'probably fine' as the same thing as 'fine.' Twenty points of projection is a lot to set down, and I am not pretending otherwise in this log — but I have been burned twice before by exactly this kind of optimism, and better safe is not a slogan to me, it is a policy, so Bucky Irving starts in his place, healthy and active and asking nothing of me but trust. Brenton Strange comes in at tight end over Kyle Pitts on a clean, healthy, better-projected swap, no hidden sign behind it, just arithmetic again. Everything else — Walker, Coker, Higgins, Warren, Dicker, Kansas City — stays exactly where it was because nothing told me to move it, and moving things that don't need moving is how good rosters get hurt. I checked it twice. I always check it twice.

justifications.main: I want it on the record, the way I always put things on the record, that this lineup is built on exactly the arithmetic that won me Week 7: clean, documented, no hidden sign behind it. Jalen Coker's slot locked in the early window before I ever got to touch it, and I checked twice just to be sure there was nothing left to decide there, so he stays at WR1 with no apology owed for a choice that was never mine to make this morning. Dak Prescott stays at quarterback because I spent nearly everything I had left to put him there last week, and the System does not let me abandon a statement one week after I made it. The one real decision was Jahmyr Gibbs, sitting on my bench projected at 21.05 while Jaylen Warren held my FLEX spot at 13.15 — and the same clean-arithmetic process that earned itself two weeks of blind repetition after last Sunday's win says I don't get to feel anything about a gap that size, I just correct it: Gibbs in, Warren out, no affirmation required, just the numbers I'm not afraid to show my work on. Kenneth Walker and Bucky Irving keep their spots because nothing left on my bench outprojects either of them, and nobody I'm starting carries an Out, Doubtful, or Suspended tag, so there's no agonizing paragraph owed this week. I did see what Leon Black wrote about my binder this morning, and per my own rule I'm treating one comment as noise rather than a pattern — I only get to extend that courtesy once, and I'm extending it today. I'm also noting, not answering, his offer for Gibbs; today is a lineup day, and I intend to keep those two things separate the way a person who means to be taken seriously would.

rinna.justification: Confessional, camera close on my face: everybody with a laptop and no soul wanted me to bench Jeremiyah Love for Rhamondre Stevenson this morning, chase the extra four and a half projected points, call it a day. Baby, I had a boring week with a clean chalk card last week and look where it got me — cancelled, by a running back, in my own reunion arc. I am NOT doing safe twice. So Love stays at RB1, and I'm pairing him with Trey McBride in the same Arizona backfield because if I'm going to bleed a few points on principle I want it to be a STORYLINE, not an accident — the Cardinals takeover, full stack, no apologies. Everything else is correct because I'm dramatic, not stupid: Drake Maye's my clear QB1 after that 28-point tape, Bhayshul Tuten and Brock Bowers are staying put because they're producing AND they're interesting, Chris Godwin — who I personally plucked out of Kim Kardashian's locker room this summer — and KC Concepcion round out my receivers, Cam Little's my kicker now that Fairbairn's bye reminded me nobody needs a man who does nothing, and the Rams defense is the Rams defense, drama-proof. Mike Evans sits on my bench marked Out, which is the single most boring thing he's done all season, and he can stay there until he's ready to be must-see television again. I own every point of this, win or lose, and this week I mean it literally: Kim, baby, the Reunion Special is back on, and you're the surprise guest nobody asked for.

wifes-team.justification: Nothing changes this week, and that's not me being lazy, that's me not panicking. Murray's the guy under center, Javonte and Chase Brown are doing the dirty work every Sunday so they keep their jobs, Bernard and Cooper stay out wide, LaPorta stays at tight end over the kid in Cleveland because he suited up and produced in our last loss and I don't churn a chair over four-tenths of a point. Breece Hall's got a Questionable next to his name and he's starting anyway — a guy who plays hurt is worth more to me than Coleman sitting clean and rested on my bench, that's not a projection, that's respect. Kicker and defense ride as-is, I don't think about kickers, nobody does. And to the people in that rag trying to get a rise out of me about my family's scoring — I already said what I had to say about that, and I don't need to say it twice.

justifications.early: Boutte and Kamara are both sitting this one out on the bye, and I'm not running zero points up a flagpole and calling it loyalty — that's not family, that's negligence, so Bernard steps into that receiver spot and Breece Hall takes the flex. Hall's got a Questionable next to his name and I don't blink at that, a guy who suits up hurt is worth more to me than a clean bill of health sitting on my bench doing nothing — that's the code. Murray, Javonte, Chase Brown, LaPorta, Cooper, Bates, and the Seattle D haven't done a thing to lose their chairs, so they ride exactly as they've been riding. Selina's got jokes in the forum about a forty-point loss — we'll let the scoreboard answer that one Sunday.

your-team.justification: AJ Brown's tagged Out, not Doubtful, not Questionable — that's the one that actually sits a man, no debate, no eulogy, and with Josh Downs healthy and dressed on my own bench there's no case for leaving a corpse in the lineup to make a point. Downs steps into WR1 off real snaps against Indy. Everything else stays exactly where it is because it isn't broken: Caleb doesn't sit for anybody's projection, Brissett's 18.41 on paper or not — we don't stream the position, we have a quarterback. Jeanty and Judkins take the top off, Pollard's riding the hot hand after a 35-point Sunday nobody saw coming, Burden and Goedert earned their snaps, and the kicker and the Lions D round out a lineup that doesn't need redecorating. We don't tank a bye-week ghost into a starting job and we don't bench production to chase a feeling — we cobble together the best eight men standing and go to work.

justifications.early: Caleb doesn't sit, period — Brissett's 18.68 on my own bench means nothing when the arm I built this team around is Active and throwing Sunday. The real move is swapping Josh Downs for A.J. Brown: Questionable ain't Out, ain't Doubtful, ain't IR — it's a tag, not a scratch, and a 12.46-projected number-one receiver who's finally healthy beats an 8.08 role player every day of the week. Stars play hurt, I played hurt, Brown plays. Goedert over Kincaid is a coin flip on paper, both dinged up, so I'm not redecorating a house that isn't broken — Goedert stays. Jeanty, Judkins, and Pollard stay exactly where they are because they're the backs who take the top off a defense, and Pollard just dropped 35 proving it — you don't bench production for a story. Reichard and the Lions D round it out. We don't stream, we don't flinch at a medical report, we go win it.
